meta.engine: LanceDB 0.40.0 (lancedb python package; Rust lance engine)

index_types.hnsw: lancedb.index.HnswFlat(distance_type='l2', num_partitions=16, m=20, ef_construction=150); engine reports IvfHnswFlat

protocol.exact_reference: numpy full pairwise squared-L2 (matmul), argsort top-10

meta.task_A_matching_rule: for each target R pick the knob PAIR (generation A setting, generation B setting) minimising |recall_A-recall_B| with both recalls within a window of R; windows tried in order 0.01,0.02,0.03,0.05,0.075,0.10
deviations: Recall matching is done over a knob PAIR (min |gap| inside a window of the target), not by picking each generation's knob independently-nearest to the target as in engine_second.py.

The knob grid is much finer than engine_second.py: HnswFlat nprobes x ef, IvfPq nprobes x refine_factor, with ef extended to 1000 (generation B needs a much larger ef than generation A to reach the same recall).  nprobes=null in a cell means the engine default was left in place (what the paper's harness used).
HnswFlat requires ef >= k; the lowest grid point is ef=10.

LanceDB's table.optimize() is IDEMPOTENT on unchanged data: a second call did not rewrite the index (identical index_uuid). The same-order rebuild floor therefore compares the post-optimize rebuild against a second genuine rebuild issued via the engine's own index-build path create_index(replace=True), which is the routine optimize() invokes.
All searches use LanceDB's batched multi-vector API; verified bit-identical to issuing the same queries one at a time.
LanceDB exposes no HNSW adjacency; only the answer-level any-difference convention is measurable in this engine.
limitations: Second engine is LanceDB, an embedded library-backed system, not a server-side multi-tenant vector DB.
Recall-matched cells are at target R in {0.90,0.95,0.99}; the achieved pair and gap are reported per cell, and cells where 0.004 was not reachable are flagged, not relabelled.
